review: Independent original PLY vertex-to-learned-material row correspondence
scope: Previously executed read-only CPU audit; no model inference or mesh conversion was executed by this reviewer.

actual_array_checks.vertex_bit_comparison: float32 arrays viewed as little-endian uint32; all rows compared in bounded 32768-row batches
actual_array_checks.coordinate_comparison: np.array_equal plus independently computed complete payload SHA256

rowwise_vertex_formula.input: c_i = geometry coordinates[i,1:]; x_i = geometry features[i,:3]
rowwise_vertex_formula.axis_order: Original [D,H,W] treated as XYZ with no permutation

static_source_review.finding: Vertex construction is rowwise. Sorting only builds a coordinate-key lookup; order[pos] maps matched neighbours back to original global vertex indices. PLY writes the complete verts array in its original order without removal, repair, or reordering.

Worker takes original coordinates[:,1:] and features; computes vertices with the audited functions, saves every vertex and face unchanged, and checks PLY and NPY readback. Duplicate-face detection sorts a separate temporary face-key buffer only. Unused vertices are retained.

The saved material path requires np.array_equal(coords, prepared['geometry_coords']); learned features are the rowwise raw*F32(.5)+F32(.5) transform with no clamp. This source was inspected as text only and was never imported or executed.

conclusion: For every original PLY vertex index i in [0,1842968), learned material feature row i corresponds to that vertex's unchanged geometry coordinate row i. No nearest-neighbour matching, coordinate sort, vertex removal, or guessed material mapping is required.
